stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorists who catalog trickster tales have found that most versions end with the trickster escaping punishment, the character's cunning rewarded by the story's close. A set of tales collected in the 1930s from fishing villages along the Baltic coast, ______, consistently ends with the trickster caught and publicly shamed, a pattern the collectors attributed to the villages' strict communal codes.
explanation: Name the subject and attribute in each sentence. Most trickster tales end with the trickster escaping. The Baltic tales end with the trickster caught. The subjects are parallel and the outcome flips, so you need a contrast word. 'By contrast' sets the Baltic tales against the general pattern.

A.why: You saw one specific collection come after a general claim and assumed it was an illustration. An example has to agree with the claim. These tales do the opposite of what most versions do, so they cannot be an instance of the pattern.

B.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that isn't there. Nothing in the first sentence produces the Baltic endings. The passage credits the villages' communal codes, not the general tendency.

D.why: You treated the sentences as a sequence in time. The passage compares two groups of tales. It does not describe one event following another.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In most temperate forests, the loss of large predators allows deer populations to grow unchecked, and heavy browsing then strips the understory of tree seedlings and wildflowers. On Hallen Island, a predator-free reserve surveyed in 2019, ______, the understory was found to be dense and species-rich, because deep winter snowpack kills off most young deer before they reach maturity.
explanation: The first sentence says that forests without predators end up with a bare understory. Hallen Island has no predators either, but its understory is dense. The situation is the same and the result is the opposite, so 'by contrast' is the logical link.

B.why: You chose an example word because a single predator-free site follows a general claim. Check the outcome first. Hallen Island's understory thrives, which goes against the tendency instead of illustrating it.

C.why: You linked predator loss to the island's condition as cause and effect. The first sentence predicts a stripped understory, and the passage explains the dense one by the snowpack, not by the general pattern.

D.why: You read the second sentence as one more point in the same direction. Try putting 'and also' between the sentences. It sounds wrong, because the island's result contradicts the first sentence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most vaccines train the immune system by presenting it with a weakened or inactivated pathogen, and many of them require several doses spaced weeks or months apart before they provide lasting protection. The vaccine for yellow fever, ______, typically confers immunity that persists for decades after a single injection, a durability researchers link to the strong and broad immune response it provokes.
explanation: Sentence one says that many vaccines need several doses. Sentence two says the yellow fever vaccine works after one. Both sentences describe vaccines, and the number of doses flips, so the contrast word 'conversely' is correct.

A.why: You called the yellow fever vaccine an example because it is one vaccine named after a claim about vaccines in general. It is the exception on the attribute that matters, dose count, so it cannot illustrate the claim.

B.why: You assumed the first sentence explains the second. Needing multiple doses doesn't cause a vaccine to work after one. The passage gives a separate reason: the strong immune response.

C.why: You read the sentences as steps in a timeline. The passage is setting two cases side by side, not describing what happens next.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many metals grow brittle as they are cooled, which is why some steel ship hulls have cracked without warning in icy northern waters. Certain austenitic stainless steels, ______, retain their toughness even at temperatures approaching absolute zero, making them the standard material for tanks that store liquefied natural gas and liquid hydrogen.
explanation: The first subject is many metals, which become brittle when cold. The second is austenitic stainless steels, which stay tough when cold. The attribute flips from brittle to tough, so 'by contrast' is the right link.

A.why: 'Similarly' only works if both subjects share the same attribute. They don't: one group grows brittle and the other stays tough. You noticed the parallel sentence frame but missed that the attribute reverses.

C.why: You took a specific type of steel to be a sample of the metals that grow brittle. These steels behave in the opposite way, so they are an exception and not an instance.

D.why: You treated the second sentence as a conclusion drawn from the first. Other metals becoming brittle does not lead to these steels staying tough.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Across most industries, workers who change employers earn larger raises than those who stay put, since competing job offers push wages upward. In public school teaching, ______, switching districts often carries a pay penalty, because many districts' salary schedules cap the number of years of prior experience a newly hired teacher can be credited with.
explanation: In most industries, switching employers raises pay. In teaching, switching districts can lower it. The two sectors are set side by side and the effect of switching reverses, so 'by contrast' fits.

A.why: Teaching is one industry, so it looks like a sample drawn from 'most industries'. Check whether it agrees with the claim. Teachers who switch lose pay rather than gain it, so teaching is the exception, not the example.

B.why: You saw a cause-and-effect link that isn't there. Raises in other industries don't produce the teachers' penalty. The passage blames salary-schedule caps.

D.why: You treated the sentence as the last step in a sequence. The passage doesn't list steps. It compares two sectors.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Nutritionists group dietary fats into several types, and most of them, including the monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats found in nuts, fish, and olive oil, tend to lower blood levels of LDL cholesterol when they replace refined carbohydrates in the diet. Trans fats, ______, raise LDL levels while also reducing HDL, the form of cholesterol associated with protection against heart disease.
explanation: The first sentence names a category, several types of fat, and says most of them lower LDL. The second gives one member of that category, trans fats, which raise LDL. Because the effect reverses, 'conversely' is the logical transition.

A.why: Trans fats are one of the 'several types', so an example word looks right. But the claim is about fats that lower LDL, and trans fats raise it. A member that breaks the pattern is a contrast, not an illustration.

C.why: 'Accordingly' means the second sentence follows from the first. Other fats lowering LDL gives no reason for trans fats to raise it.

D.why: You heard the second sentence as more of the same because it also reports a cholesterol effect. The effect runs the opposite way, so 'and also' doesn't fit between the sentences.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In most large concrete structures, engineers embed steel reinforcing bars wherever the material will be stretched under load, since concrete withstands compression well but cracks easily under tension. The dome of the Pantheon in Rome, ______, contains no steel at all: its curved shape keeps nearly the entire structure in compression, and it has stood for almost nineteen centuries.
explanation: The first sentence says large concrete structures rely on embedded steel. The Pantheon's dome is a large concrete structure with no steel. The attribute flips from reinforced to unreinforced, so 'in contrast' is correct.

B.why: The Pantheon is a famous large concrete structure, so it seems like a natural example. But the claim is that such structures use steel, and the dome doesn't. It is an exception, not an illustration.

C.why: You read the second sentence as a conclusion. Engineers reinforcing most structures doesn't lead to the Pantheon lacking steel. The passage credits the dome's shape.

D.why: You took the passage to be describing construction steps. It compares a general practice with one structure that departs from it. There is no sequence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In most North American cities, zoning codes separate land uses, placing homes, shops, and offices in distinct districts so that residents often must drive from one to another. Houston, ______, has never adopted a citywide zoning code, and houses, stores, and small workshops can legally stand side by side on a single block, although private deed restrictions limit such mixing in some neighborhoods.
explanation: Most North American cities use zoning to separate land uses. Houston has no citywide zoning, so uses can mix. The two sentences set parallel cities side by side with the attribute reversed, so 'by contrast' is the logical choice.

A.why: Houston is a North American city, so it looks like a sample of the group. Check whether it matches the general claim. Houston lacks the zoning the other cities have, which makes it an exception, not an instance.

B.why: You treated Houston's lack of zoning as a result of the first sentence. Other cities' zoning practices don't cause Houston's policy.

C.why: You read the second sentence as more support for the first. It describes the opposite arrangement. The 'and also' test fails, so an addition word is wrong.
